title: Ka'ba-ye Zartosht
visualBrief: Surviving limestone tower at Naqsh-e Rustam with engaged corners, shallow staggered recesses, dark false windows, 17-dentil cornices, broken access flight and low pyramidal stone roof.

nativeAxes.origin: Measured tower center on original/excavated floor; Y=0 excludes the modern surrounding excavation grade.

scaleBasis: Schmidt / Oriental Institute field measurements and elevations, Persepolis III (1970), figures 5-15 and pp. 35-37. Surviving eight-step remnant is retained; the hypothetical complete thirty-step stair is excluded.

geographicProposal.evidence: Schmidt1970 printedp34 explicitly gives the tower main axis18degrees west of north. Native+Z is the surviving north doorway/stair; native+X runs west-southwest. Inspected north-up Google satellite at29.9884865,52.8740303 corroborates the broken entrance facing the cliffNNW and the center inside the excavated perimeter. Heading-162degrees follows the published axis with about3degrees reconstruction uncertainty. The retainedOSM exact-QID center is approximate; newOSM/Overpass reads returned429, so no fresh outline or survey is claimed.
geographicProposal.limitations: Static medium-fi exterior based on Schmidt1970 measured elevations/plans and inspected2010/2016 photographs. Original14038-triangle draft remains unchanged. Reviewed source adds jagged stair scar, raised eight-step remnant/rubble and the north roof slab displaced60cm at its west end.14.12m maximum height/7.30m nominal side retain measured original dimensions; slight settled/sloping base differences are simplified. Eight preserved original steps are distinguished from missing original lower/upper access; stair datum1.08m and rubble shapes are approximate. Twenty-one large-block courses average irregular historic jointing; local repairs/cracks and exact engravedGreek/Parthian/Pahlavi text are omitted rather than fabricated. Roof cramp marks are original geometric indications, not a measured cavity survey. Hidden chamber, buried foundations, detached archaeological fragments, modern railings and the entire excavation cut are outside the individual monument exterior. The host terrain must supply the excavated floor datum; a coarse surrounding-gradeDEM will bury the base. Ground0 does not certify the hostDEM or site cut. Footprint replacement disabled.

appearance.identity: Surviving pale-limestone square tower, two engaged corner piers per face, dark false windows, shallow staggered recesses, seventeen cornice dentils per face, broken north staircase/doorway and low four-slab pyramid roof.
appearance.master: Reviewed source-local exterior; original draft preserved.
appearance.browser: Complete square tower, stepped base, false windows, cornice and low displaced roof at every level; physical shallow recesses at street/closeup. Pale and dark stones share one raw-limestone grain graph; false-window frames retain original dark vertex tint without fabricated mortar.
